# Open assumptions (/assumptions)



| Question                                         | What we're assuming now                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | When we close it                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Are crying and heart rate linked?                | We treat them as two separate signs of the same stress, not as one causing the other. So S3 does not expect one to directly change the other.                                                                                                                                                                     | At Demo 1, on the digital twin: we look at both signals together and check whether they move together more than the model says. If they do, S3 will weigh them accordingly. |
| How do we drive the motors?                      | S4 sends the two 1 kHz PWM signals (rocking speed and rocking strength) on the motor connections of the board. The cradle setup gives the motors their power.                                                                                                                                                     | First cradle time slot, before Demo 1: we measure the load (must stay above 0.8 A) and the duty (must stay under 90%).                                                      |
| Can the timers keep up?                          | We build on the fixed PYNQ Z2 board: its UART and I2C for the communication, its general-purpose timers for the 1 kHz PWM signals. We assume the timers can keep both PWM signals at exactly 1 kHz with stable duty, even while the communication code runs.                                                      | First bring-up: we check both signals on the oscilloscope, before Demo 1.                                                                                                   |
| Do the two measurements arrive at the same time? | Each sensor board cleans up its own signal first: S1 sends a ready BPM value (with trend) at 2 Hz, S2 sends the filtered cry level at 10 Hz. So S3 combines two finished values, not raw waves. The open point: the two values must arrive close enough together for S3 to combine them at 1 decision per second. | COMM-2 test (Section 2.4): we measure how long each signal takes to arrive. S3 writes a timestamp on both values, so if one is late, it shows up on the LCD.                |


# Communication (/communication)









The four PYNQ boards sit in the cradle backbone and exchange heartbeat, crying, decision, and command signals. Two topologies are under evaluation.

## Full system [#full-system]

<img alt="Full system block diagram" src="__img0" />

The cradle sensors (photo detector, mic) feed S1 and S2; S1 and S2 send SIG_HR and SIG_CR to S3; S3 sends SIG_CMD to S4; S4 drives the cradle motors with two 1 kHz PWM signals.

## Option 1: shared UART line [#option-1-shared-uart-line]

<img alt="Option 1: shared UART line" src="__img1" />

Every board has its own TX and RX on the backbone, plus a common ground. UART is point-to-point, so addressing and turn-taking are built on top of it: each board gets a 4-bit address and every frame carries a destination.

## Option 2: I2C link [#option-2-i2c-link]

<img alt="Option 2: I2C link" src="__img2" />

One shared data wire (SDA) and one clock wire (SCL) with a common ground. S3 acts as the master, S1, S2 and S4 as slaves. Addressing is built into the protocol, so no frame header is needed.

# Overview (/)





**Rock your Baby - Team 34**

A controller that reads a baby's heart rate and crying, decides a rocking motion, and drives a cradle. Four PYNQ Z2 boards, one communication backbone, one cradle.

| Field        |                     |
| ------------ | ------------------- |
| **Team**     | 34 · 9 members      |
| **Board**    | PYNQ Z2 (Zynq-7020) |
| **Document** | v1.4 · Sections 1+2 |
| **Updated**  | 12 October 2026     |

| ------------------ | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| ✅ **Done**         | Sections 1-2 in the design document | Requirements, architecture, communication protocol |
| 🔶 **In progress** | Section 3 design description        | Per-submodule design, S1-S4                        |
| ⬜ **Next**         | Board bring-up                      | Hardware time slots, 1 kHz PWM + comm verification |

# Submodules (/submodules)





## S1 Heartbeat [#s1-heartbeat]

Extracts heart rate from the LED signal; conditions its own signal before sending.

Status: In design

## S2 Crying [#s2-crying]

Detects and filters cry level from the microphone signal.

Status: In design

## S3 Decision [#s3-decision]

Fuses the two processed values into a (frequency, amplitude) decision; timestamps both inputs so misalignment shows on the LCD.

Status: In design

<Callout type="info">
  TODO: circuit will be added
</Callout>

## S4 Motor drivers [#s4-motor-drivers]

Converts the (F, A) decision into two 1 kHz PWM signals on the motor-control connections; cradle supplies motor power.

Status: In design
